_doc: T-1333 acceptance 2: the frozen readings the closing accounting states its deltas AGAINST. A count with no baseline is not a delta, and a baseline recomputed from git history is not reproducible in a shallow clone — so each reading is taken once, at a named commit, and committed here. tools/report_convergence_closing.py reads this file and NEVER rewrites it.
_how_taken: Check the named commit out into a worktree, copy tools/report_convergence_closing.py into it, and call build()['measures'] — the same code that measures the live tree, so the two ends of every delta are measured the same way. Recorded readings carry their own command instead.
_the_rule: A baseline row is FROZEN. It is a reading of a tree that existed, and it is never re-derived, re-fitted or quietly corrected: if it was wrong it is wrong in the record, and a later row says so. Adding a measure to the report leaves the older baselines silent on it, which the report prints as `not measured then` rather than as a zero — a zero would be a claim nobody made.

baselines.what: The tree T-1144 opened on — the last commit of 2026-09-15, the day the parent ticket was written and its opening measurement taken. This is the baseline the CONVERGENCE is measured against.
